data.name: DiscriminatedUnionDeclarationNotFoundDescription
data.value: Happens when a discriminated union cannot be found. Maybe it was declare in a different project?

data.name: DiscriminatedUnionDeclarationNotFoundMessageFormat
data.value: The discriminated union {1} for the case {0} was missing

data.name: DiscriminatedUnionDeclarationNotFoundTitle
data.value: Discriminated Union declaration was not found

data.name: StructUnionMustBePartialStructDescription
data.value: The members of a struct union are generated in another part of the struct, so the struct must be partial. Record structs and ref structs are not supported, because they come with members that conflict with the generated ones.

data.name: StructUnionMustBePartialStructMessageFormat
data.value: The struct union {0} must be declared as a partial struct that is neither a record struct nor a ref struct

data.name: StructUnionMustBePartialStructTitle
data.value: Struct unions must be partial structs

data.name: StructUnionCasesAreAllReferenceTypesDescription
data.value: A struct union exists to avoid boxing cases that are structs. When every case is a reference type nothing is boxed, and a union declaration is a single reference in size where a struct union needs a tag in addition. No members are generated for such a struct union.

data.name: StructUnionCasesAreAllReferenceTypesMessageFormat
data.value: All cases of the struct union {0} are reference types ({1}): declare it as a union instead, which stores a reference case without allocating and is smaller

data.name: StructUnionCasesAreAllReferenceTypesTitle
data.value: A union declaration is the better choice when all cases are reference types

data.name: StructUnionHasMultipleDefaultCasesDescription
data.value: The default case is the case that the default value of the union represents, so there can only be one. Declare the other cases with ICase.

data.name: StructUnionHasMultipleDefaultCasesMessageFormat
data.value: The struct union {0} declares more than one default case: {1}

data.name: StructUnionHasMultipleDefaultCasesTitle
data.value: Struct unions can only have one default case

data.name: StructUnionDefaultCaseHasPayloadDescription
data.value: The default value of a struct union has no values to give the default case, so the default case cannot have any. Declare the case with ICase to get a union whose default value has no value.

data.name: StructUnionDefaultCaseHasPayloadMessageFormat
data.value: The default case {1} of the struct union {0} must be a struct without instance fields

data.name: StructUnionDefaultCaseHasPayloadTitle
data.value: The default case of a struct union must be a struct without instance fields

data.name: StructUnionCaseIsTypeParameterDescription
data.value: Cases are told apart by their type. A type parameter can be substituted by the type of another case, in which case the two could not be told apart.

data.name: StructUnionCaseIsTypeParameterMessageFormat
data.value: The type parameter {1} cannot be a case of the struct union {0}: wrap it in a case type

data.name: StructUnionCaseIsTypeParameterTitle
data.value: A type parameter cannot be a case of a struct union

data.name: UnionCannotBeSegregatedDescription
data.value: The types that segregate a union are declared in the namespace of the union. From there they have to refer to the union and to each of its cases, which they cannot when one of those is private or protected within a type, or when the union and a type it is nested in have a type parameter of the same name.

data.name: UnionCannotBeSegregatedMessageFormat
data.value: The union {0} cannot be segregated, because the types that segregate it could not refer to {1} from the namespace of the union

data.name: UnionCannotBeSegregatedTitle
data.value: A union that is segregated and its cases must be accessible from the namespace of the union
